summary: Intermittent p95/p99 latency chords during steady traffic due to connection-keepalive shear in continuous batching pipeline
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent spikes in p95/p99 latency that appear as short, repeating 'chords' (groups of elevated tails) during otherwise steady traffic patterns. Spikes are correlated with streaming and short-sequence generation paths served by the continuous batching pipeline.

Impact:
- Affected LuminaHealth production cluster in us-east-1 (dedicated).
- Client saw increased 504/timeouts and degraded UX for short chat completions during several 10-30s windows.
- Noticeable at p95 and p99; median/mean unaffected.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted dedicated pool (dedicated tenant).
- Region: us-east-1.
- Models: rw-13b-v1 primary, fallback opt-6.7b.
- Traffic: steady low-per-connection QPS from long-lived HTTP/2 connections (keepalive enabled).

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Maintain ~8 QPS per connection across 200 connections to a single route pinned to rw-13b-v1.
2) Allow connections to remain idle ~30s between bursts; keepalive at client set to 60s.
3) Observe p95/p99 metric on route-level dashboard and streaming traces.

Observed behavior:
- Periodic p95/p99 spikes that align to multi-second boundaries (appears as clustered 'chords').
- Traces show many requests waiting in continuous-batcher pools with near-identical enqueue timestamps, then flush together.
- KV-cache warm hits slightly higher during spikes; a small fraction of requests receive 504/timeouts.

Expected behavior:
- Smooth p95/p99 without synchronized clusters; continuous batcher should avoid alignment that amplifies tail latency.

Initial logs and links:
- Datadog dashboard: https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/xx/luminahealth-latency-route
- Error traces (sample): https://sentry.redwoodinc/issue/ae34f
- Customer-provided gRPC client logs attached via support upload (s3 link pinned in ticket).
comments: 2026-03-10 - LuminaHealth (Jonas Reiss): We see user complaints starting ~2026-03-10T08:20Z. P95 jumps from ~150ms baseline to 800-1200ms for 10-25s. Attached traces and client keepalive config.
2026-03-10 - Support (Emily Chen): Acknowledged and triaged to SRE. Gathering traces, adding instrumentation to track enqueue timestamps in batcher. Assigned to Ravi.

2026-03-11 - SRE (Ravi Kumar): Initial look at traces: requests have tightly clustered enqueue timestamps (within 10-30ms). Hypothesis: connection-keepalive alignment causes synchronized micro-bursts that the continuous batcher doesn't jitter, leading to enhanced tail amplification.
2026-03-11 - LuminaHealth (Jonas Reiss): We can schedule a controlled test with jittered client keepalives. Will run tonight and report back.

2026-03-12 - SRE (Ravi Kumar): Ran internal repro by forcing 200 connections with keepalive aligned. Reproduced p99 chords. Temporary mitigation tested by enabling per-connection enqueue jitter and adding a small randomization to the batch-flush timer. p99 reduced by ~85% in canary run.
2026-03-12 - Support (Emily Chen): Communicated mitigation to customer and requested permission for staged rollout. LuminaHealth approved.
investigation_notes: Metric pattern: periodic clusters at ~30-60s cadence; cluster width 2-6s. Median unaffected, tails amplify when batches flush synchronously.
Hypothesis A: Client keepalive timers causing alignment of request arrival and thus batcher flush alignment (keepalive shear).
Hypothesis B: KV-cache prefetch/backpressure briefly increases enqueue latency in a way that nudges tenants into the same flush window (less likely based on cache hit rates).
Experiment 1: Simulated 200 steady connections with identical keepalive interval -> reproduced chorded p99 spikes (PRF).
Experiment 2: Introduced randomized per-connection small jitter (5-50ms) to enqueue timestamp -> reduced alignment and lowered p99 dramatically.
Experiment 3: Implemented optional batch-flush timer jitter in serving runtime (canary) -> similar reduction at route-level in us-east-1 canary.
Related signals: small bump in KV-cache misses during chords; increased scheduler queue length for short-lived microbatches.
Logs: repeated pattern of logs 'coalescer: flush window closed at t; queued: 187; median-wait: 48ms' during chords.
Link to internal runbook section updated: add detection rule for 'enqueue-skew' and a dashboard panel showing enqueue timestamp variance per-tenant.
resolution:
Workaround and permanent fix applied:
- Short-term workaround: recommended customer to enable random jitter on client keepalive within their SDK (documented steps provided). This provided immediate relief during their test window.
- Code fix: implemented randomized batch-flush jitter and per-connection enqueue jitter in serving runtime (PR https://github.com/redwood/serving/pull/981). Also added metric 'enqueue_timestamp_variance' and an alert when variance < 200ms and p99 increases.
- Rollout plan: canary in us-east-1 (LuminaHealth cluster) on 2026-03-12 -> observed ~85-90% reduction in p99 spike amplitude and eliminated 504s in observed windows. Gradual rollout to other regions over 48 hours.
- Post-action: updated continuous-batcher runbook and added follow-up task INT-1123 to add synthetic test coverage for keepalive-aligned scenarios.

Notes for CS/SRE: mark customer SR as resolved after 48h of stable metrics; customer to confirm SLA impact window for closure.
